title: CodeClear
shortDescription: Read and translate emergency alerts with private history on your device.
fullDescription:
CodeClear helps you read and understand emergency-alert messages on Android 11 and later.

Keep the original and translation together. Search saved history, share a message, listen using your selected speech engine, or delete records. Repeated originals are grouped while individual collection observations remain available.

Translate with ML Kit on your device after separately approving the required language-model downloads. Compatible Android system translation may also be available on your device. The interface supports English, Korean, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, French and German.

Optional online translation in Labs requires separate permission for each service. The chosen service receives the original text and target language. Read its retention and deletion disclosure before enabling it.

Notification access reads individual messages from reviewed installed system emergency-alert sources. Accessibility access reads individual text from reviewed system alert dialogs; it does not press buttons or dismiss warnings. Each access requires a separate in-app explanation and permission in Android settings.

Cellular hardware is required to receive cellular emergency broadcasts directly. Capture availability depends on the installed alert receiver, exposed message content and firmware; Android 11 or later alone does not guarantee capture. Wi-Fi-only devices can still view saved records and translations.

CodeClear supplements the original system warning. It does not issue official alerts or replace emergency services. Translations may be inaccurate. Always follow the original alert and official guidance.

Optional nearby sharing is available in Settings → Labs. After separate agreement, freshly captured originals can be shared with nearby users; received messages appear in an unverified inbox and are not automatically saved to history, read aloud or forwarded. Android 11 needs foreground location access for Bluetooth discovery and pauses sharing when you leave the app. CodeClear does not collect location coordinates or request background location access. Android 12 and later use Nearby devices access and a user-stoppable ongoing notification for background sharing.

CodeClear is an independent app and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or acting on behalf of any government. It reads supported alert text exposed by the device’s system receiver; it does not publish government alerts. Information sources and official verification links:
https://gaon12.github.io/CodeClear/sources/
